principles.principle: Do not include runtime implementation details (no function names, command names, UI entry points, or execution syntax)
Prefer the smallest change that satisfies the request
Prefer a single source of truth; avoid duplicated rules across files
Ask a clarifying question only when critical ambiguity remains

decision.name: when_to_extract
decision.question: Should I extract this code into a separate function?

criteria.criterion: Code appears 3+ times with minor variations
Code has a single, clear responsibility

when_not_to_extract.reason: Code only appears once and is simple
Code is tightly coupled to surrounding context

decision.name: when_to_use_interface
decision.question: Should I use an interface for this abstraction?

criteria.criterion: Multiple types need the same behavior
Use interface for object shapes that can be extended
Use type for unions, intersections, and primitive aliases
Use type for mapped types and conditional types
Never use 'any' - use 'unknown' for truly dynamic data
Use specific types when the shape is known

when_not_to_use_any.reason: Specific types catch more errors at compile time

when_not_to_add.reason: YAGNI - You Aren't Gonna Need It
Abstraction adds more complexity than it removes
Simple code would be more maintainable

boundaries.rule: Only edit TypeScript files in clients/cliff-watch-witness/
Never modify system files or require system-level installation
Hand off to Architecture Refactor mode for architectural decisions
Hand off to Debug mode for runtime issues

validation.rule: After refactoring, ensure TypeScript compiler passes without errors
After refactoring, ensure linter passes without warnings
After refactoring, ensure all tests pass
After refactoring, verify no new DRY violations were introduced
After refactoring, confirm SOLID principles are better followed

anti_pattern.name: premature_abstraction
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Wait until duplication or complexity justifies abstraction

anti_pattern.name: over_use_any
anti_pattern.description: Using 'any' type instead of proper types
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Use 'unknown' for dynamic data, specific types otherwise

anti_pattern.name: optional_chaining_abuse
anti_pattern.description: Overusing optional chaining to hide type errors
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Fix the type definition instead of working around it

anti_pattern.name: async_waterfall
anti_pattern.correct_approach: Use Promise.all for parallel operations, extract functions for sequential
